tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Accounting – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: Which accounting concept is violated when a proprietor pays his son's school fees from the business bank account and debits it to expenses?
options: Money measurement concept, as the fees cannot be measured
Business entity concept, as personal and business affairs are mixed
Cost concept, as the asset is not shown at its original cost
Going concern concept, as continuity of the firm is doubted
questions.explanation: Personal expenses of the owner are drawings, not business expenses.

questions.question_text: A firm buys goods for Rs 50,000 but they have a market value of Rs 60,000 on the same date. The goods are recorded at Rs 50,000 on the basis of:
questions.explanation: Assets are recorded at the price paid.

questions.question_text: Rent paid in advance for the next year is shown as an asset because of:
options: Materiality concept, minor expenses are written off at once
Cash concept, expenses are recorded when they are paid
Accrual concept, expenses are matched to the period they relate to
Consistency concept, the same method is followed every year
questions.explanation: Prepaid portion is a benefit yet to be received.

questions.question_text: Closing stock is valued at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower. This follows the convention of:
questions.explanation: Anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses.

questions.question_text: A firm changes its method of depreciation every year to show better profits. This violates the convention of:
options: Materiality, which allows trivial items to be ignored
Conservatism, which requires provision for expected losses
Full disclosure, which requires all material facts to be stated
Consistency, which requires the same methods over periods

questions.question_text: Pencils worth Rs 200 purchased by a large firm are charged to expense, not shown as stock. This is justified by the convention of:
questions.explanation: Insignificant items need not be separately recorded as assets.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the going concern concept?
options: The business earns profit in each of the periods
The business is assumed to continue for an indefinite period
The business will be wound up at the end of every year
The business will be sold at its current market value
questions.explanation: Basis for treating fixed assets as long-term.

questions.question_text: Under the dual aspect concept, every transaction has:
options: Two effects, which both increase the assets
Effects only on the capital and the profits
A single effect on the total of the assets
Two equal and opposite effects on the accounts

questions.question_text: Which of the following transactions will NOT change the total of the assets?
options: Receipt of cash from a debtor
questions.explanation: One asset is exchanged for another.

questions.question_text: Assets Rs 3,00,000 and outside liabilities Rs 1,20,000. Capital as per the accounting equation is:
A firm has capital of Rs 2,00,000 and liabilities of Rs 2,00,000. It borrows Rs 50,000 and uses it to buy machinery. Total assets now are:
questions.explanation: Assets and liabilities both rise by 50,000.

questions.question_text: Purchase of goods on credit worth Rs 8,000 will:
options: Increase assets and capital by Rs 8,000 each
Decrease liabilities and assets by Rs 8,000 each
Increase assets and decrease liabilities by Rs 8,000
Increase assets and liabilities by Rs 8,000 each

questions.question_text: Payment of Rs 5,000 to a creditor will:
options: Reduce both the assets and the liabilities by Rs 5,000
Leave the assets and liabilities unchanged
Reduce the capital and the assets by Rs 5,000
Reduce only the liabilities by Rs 5,000

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a real account?
Salaries outstanding account is classified as:
questions.explanation: Represents the amount payable to employees, a liability.

questions.question_text: Commission received in advance is:
options: An income of the current period only
A liability, being income received but not yet earned
An asset, being cash received from a customer
An expense of the next period

questions.question_text: According to the modern rule, the rule for debit and credit for an increase in liabilities is:
questions.explanation: Increase in liability is a credit.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a capital expenditure?
questions.explanation: Cost of putting the asset in working condition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a revenue expenditure?
options: Purchase of land for the factory
questions.explanation: Benefits for a single accounting period.

questions.question_text: Legal expenses incurred on the purchase of a building are:
options: Charged to profit and loss as revenue expense
Shown as drawings of the proprietor
Capitalised as part of the cost of building

questions.question_text: Heavy advertising expenditure with benefits spread over 3 years is:
questions.explanation: Benefit extends beyond the current period.

questions.question_text: Sale of old machinery for Rs 30,000 (book value Rs 25,000) gives a:
options: Capital receipt of Rs 30,000 and a gain of Rs 5,000
Revenue loss of Rs 5,000 on the sale
Capital loss of Rs 5,000 on the sale
Revenue receipt of Rs 30,000 as part of sales
questions.explanation: Sale of a fixed asset is a capital receipt.

questions.question_text: Interest received on investments is a:
questions.explanation: Earned in the course of the business.

questions.question_text: Accounting Standards in India are issued by the:
questions.explanation: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.

questions.question_text: Which user of accounting information is MOST interested in the long-term solvency of a firm?
questions.explanation: Their funds are at risk for a long period.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the main objective of financial accounting?
options: To find out frauds and errors in the books
To determine profit and show the financial position
To help managers plan the future budgets
To determine the cost per unit of every product

questions.question_text: Management accounting differs from financial accounting in that it:
options: Is meant for internal use by the management
Follows only the GAAP rules strictly
Relates to the past events only
Is compulsory under the Companies Act

questions.question_text: Cost accounting is concerned with:
options: Recording of the transactions at market value
Preparation of the statutory reports for the owners
Verification of books by the independent auditors
Ascertainment and control of the costs of production

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a limitation of accounting?
options: It records all the transactions of the business
It gives exact values for the future events
It records only the transactions that can be measured in money
It is free of the bias of the persons preparing it

questions.question_text: Under the cash basis of accounting:
options: Transactions are recorded when cash is received or paid
Transactions are recorded when they are agreed

questions.question_text: Under the accrual basis, an expense is recognised when:
options: It is paid in cash to the supplier
It is approved by the management
It is incurred, whether or not cash is paid

questions.question_text: Salary of Rs 12,000 for December is paid in January. In the accounts for the year ending 31 December it is:
options: Recorded as an expense and a liability
Ignored until it is paid in January

questions.question_text: Revenue is recognised when goods are sold even if cash is not received, due to the:
questions.explanation: Sale is complete when title passes.

questions.question_text: The accounting period concept requires that:
options: Accounts be closed only when the business is closed
Accounts be prepared once in five years

Profit be calculated only on dissolution

questions.question_text: The "entity" concept says that:
options: The business is treated as separate from its owner
The owner is liable for the debts of the business
The personal assets are shown in the balance sheet
The business ends with the death of the owner

questions.question_text: The proprietor takes goods worth Rs 3,000 for personal use. The entry is:
Owner's capital as per the business is a liability to the business because of the:
questions.explanation: It is owed to the proprietor.

questions.question_text: The balance sheet is a statement of:
options: Receipts and payments for a period of time
Assets, liabilities and capital at a point of time
Incomes and expenses for a period of time
Debits and credits for a period of time

questions.question_text: The profit and loss account shows:
options: The cash balance on a date
The results of operations over a period
The trial balance on a date
The financial position on a date

options: Omission of the previous year's data
Frequent changes in the accounting methods

questions.question_text: The matching concept requires that:
options: Expenses are matched against the revenues they helped earn
Assets are matched against the liabilities of the firm
Cash receipts are matched with the cash payments
Debits are matched with credits on the same date
questions.explanation: Determination of the profit for the period.

questions.question_text: Self-generated goodwill is not recorded in the books because of:
options: The going concern concept of the business
The business entity concept of the firm
The matching concept of revenue and cost

questions.question_text: The skill and honesty of employees is not recorded in the books due to:
Which of these is NOT a branch of accounting?
questions.explanation: It is a function of management.
